messages.subject: iid model priori
parts:
Hi guys, 

do I understand the documentation correctly? From my point of view it says that the following code assumes that the parameter year is assumed to be normally distributed with zero mean and precision parameter $\tau$ that is again Gamma-distributed, right? Would it be possible to define a priori for this precision that is inverse-gamma distributed, such that the actual variance of the normal distribution is gamma distributed?

prec.prior.year <- list(prec = list(prior = "", param = c(0.1, 0.1)))

model <- inla(y ~ f(year, model = "rw1", hyper = prec.prior.year), family = "poisson", data = data)

Best

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] iid model priori
parts:
Hi, you understand this correct. I do not recommend in general Gamma()
priors for precision any more,

https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1491465621

but if you want inv-Gamma, you can do that yourself: see

> inla.doc("table:")
> inla.doc("expression:")


just note that you need to return the log prior for the log precision,
so you need the compute the jacobian when you change variable

H
